# sindr

> Analog circuit simulator in pure Rust: a SPICE-style modified nodal analysis (MNA) solver with built-in semiconductor device models. Build a `Circuit` (a list of `CircuitElement`s plus a ground node name, optionally with blocks and instances) in Rust or JSON, or parse a SPICE3 subset, then run DC operating point, transient (Gear-2 by default, or trapezoidal or backward Euler), AC small-signal, noise (`.noise`), transfer function (`.tf`), DC sensitivity (`.sens`), DC sweep or temperature sweep. Two crates: `sindr` (the solver and the `Circuit` data model with its design hierarchy) and `sindr-devices` (device companion models). Version 0.1: plain 0.x until 1.0, where a minor bump is breaking.

Key facts for generating code:

- `solve_op(&circuit)` is SPICE's `.op`: capacitors open, inductors shorted, each waveform source at its t = 0 value. `solve_circuit` runs DC, or a transient (and reports its end state) when the circuit has capacitors, inductors or waveform sources. Neither runs AC: use `solve_ac(&circuit, &AcConfig::new("V1", f_start, f_stop, num_points))`. `dc_sweep` solves each point as `solve_op` does.
- Analysis configs are built with constructors and `with_*` setters, never struct literals: `AcConfig::new(..).with_phase_deg(..)`, `NoiseConfig::new(output, input_source, f_start, f_stop, num_points)`, `TfConfig::new(TfOutput::voltage("out"), "V1")`, `SensConfig::new(..)`, `TransientConfig::new(tstop, tstep)`. Tolerances, iteration budget and a nodeset go in `Solver::new(SolverOptions::default().with_nodeset(..))`, which has a method per analysis.
- `CircuitElement`, `Waveform`, the result types and the error enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`: a `match` on them needs a `_ =>` arm. Model and parameter structs (`DiodeModel`, `BjtModel`, `Part`, `sindr::devices::*Params`) are filled with `..Default::default()`.
- `solve_circuit` picks the transient duration and step from the circuit's time constants (5 τ, τ/50). To set them, as SPICE's `.tran` does, call `solve_transient(&circuit, &TransientConfig::new(tstop, tstep))`. Steps never exceed `tstep`; the stepper adds shorter ones where accuracy or a waveform edge needs them, so snapshot counts vary.
- Node order: BJT `[base, collector, emitter]`, MOSFET and JFET `[gate, drain, source]`, IGBT `[gate, collector, emitter]`, op-amp `[in_plus, in_minus, out]`. Voltage source `nodes[0]` is the positive terminal.
- Every node needs a DC path to ground, and one node must equal `Circuit::ground_node`.
- `VoltageRegulator` (`[input, output, gnd]`) is a linear regulator: `model: Some(RegulatorParams::lm7805())` / `::ams1117()` adds dropout, quiescent current, current limit and line/load regulation; `None` is ideal. Its result is the pass element (`Vin − Vout`, output current, dissipation).
- Self-heating: `Part::thermal` (`Thermal::junction_to_ambient(rθja)`, `Thermal::on_heatsink(rθjc, rθca)`, optional `cth`, `ambient` in K) heats that part's junction by its dissipation in `solve_circuit`/`solve_transient`. Junction temperatures are in `SimulationResult::junction_temperatures`; no balance is `SimError::ThermalRunaway`.
- `check_ratings(&circuit, &result)` checks each part against the absolute maximum `Ratings` on its `Part` (`circuit.parts`), at the operating point or every transient step, with worst value, time and margin. Missing ratings report `Unverified`, never a pass.
- `check_specs(&result, &specs)` (`sindr::measure`) takes `Measurement`s (value at x, min/max/avg/RMS/pp, `WHEN` crossings, `TRIG`/`TARG` delay, rise/fall, settling, −3 dB) on any result and judges each `Spec` (min/max limits): value, pass/fail, margin, and the reason when unmeasured. `SpecReport::with_ratings` adds the ratings checks. SPICE `.meas` cards parse into `ParsedNetlist::measurements`.
- `SwitchSpdt { nodes: [common, a, b], position: SpdtPosition::A | B }`, `Crystal { params: CrystalParams::from_datasheet(freq, esr, c0) }` and `FerriteBead { params: FerriteBeadParams::from_datasheet(z_100mhz, r_dc) }` are solved as networks of simpler elements, with results under their own id. A crystal is open at DC; its `power` is the drive level.
- `sindr::import` maps a schematic tool's netlist onto sindr: `Netlist { components: [Component::new(id, ComponentKind::Resistor).with_value("4k7")], nets: [Net::new(id, [(component, terminal)])] }` plus a `Bench` (ground, `BenchSource`s and `BenchLoad`s on nets or terminals, ties, `Analysis`), run by `import::simulate`. Terminals match by name (`anode`/`cathode`, `B`/`C`/`E`, `G`/`D`/`S`, `in+`/`in-`/`out`; `1`/`2` on unpolarised parts). Values read like a schematic (`1M` is mega, `4k7` is 4.7 k). Results and `ImportError`s use the caller's ids. Power-port names drive nothing unless `Bench::with_supplies_from_net_names` is called.
- SI units throughout (V, A, Ω, F, H, s, K). Junction temperatures are in kelvin; 300.15 K is nominal.
- Device models: Shockley diodes, Ebers–Moll BJT, Level-1 MOSFET, square-law JFET and IGBT. No BSIM or Gummel–Poon. `.model` cards fill diode IS/N/RS/CJO/VJ/M/FC/TT/BV/IBV/KF/AF and BJT IS/BF/BR/NF/NR/VAF/KF/AF (`DiodeModel`, `BjtModel`); other parameters are rejected (strict) or warned about. SPICE input (feature `spice`) reads R, L, C, V, I, D, Q, B (`V={expr}`/`I={expr}`, E/G `VALUE={expr}` and E/G/F/H `POLY(n)`, into `CircuitElement::Behavioural`), X, linear E/G/F/H and K (two `L` lines into one `Transformer`) elements, plus `.ic`/`.nodeset` into `ParsedNetlist::{initial_conditions, nodesets}`. V/I lines take `[DC] v`, `AC mag [phase]` and a waveform in any order; `ParsedNetlist::ac_config()` drives a deck's `.ac` from its own `AC` source, and `.ac`/`.noise` sweep ngspice's frequency grid. `spice::to_netlist(&Circuit, title)` writes a deck back out (R, L, C, V, I, D, Q, B, E/G/F/H, K and exact R/D equivalents; other elements are an `ExportError`); `parse_str` reads it back.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/README.md): workspace overview
- [sindr README](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/sindr/README.md): every `CircuitElement`, analyses, results, JSON format
- [sindr-devices README](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/sindr-devices/README.md): device models and companion functions
- [LIMITATIONS](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/LIMITATIONS.md): what sindr does not do; read this before assuming a feature exists
- [sindr on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/sindr): API reference, with a capability table on the front page
- [sindr-devices on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/sindr-devices): device model API reference
- [llms-full.txt](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/llms-full.txt): all of the above plus the public API and examples in one file

## Examples

- [Examples directory](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/tree/main/sindr/examples): one small program per capability (voltage divider, BJT amplifier, transient RC, Bode plot, transfer function, sensitivity, DC sweep, temperature sweep, initial voltages, schematic netlist import, SPICE netlist)
